errors.quote: Arm B positive:** the compound inhibits the reporter enzyme.
errors.issue: Arm B uses fluorescence and can remain positive from optical or reporter-substrate chemistry effects. The preceding measurements do not independently establish reporter catalysis; the categorical enzyme attribution is unsupported.

errors.quote: at minimum, inner-filter artifact is present.
errors.issue: Arm A signal loss without enzymes establishes fluorophore/detection interference, not specifically inner filtering. Chemical loss or quenching must remain alternatives.

This is insufficient to classify noncompetitive or other intrinsic target inhibition. Finite substrate range, slow/tight binding, substrate/product chemistry and assay precision matter; a full validated matrix is required.

errors.quote: LC-MS is preferred because it is unaffected by both D2 (coupling enzyme) and D3 (absorbance).
errors.issue: It bypasses those specific mechanisms but can have compound-dependent ion suppression or analyte loss. A standard curve through quench alone is not compound-matched recovery validation; product/substrate chemical stability controls are missing.

The conversion requires the specified reversible competitive model, initial rates and negligible inhibitor depletion. Those applicability checks are not adequately provided; a rightward shift alone does not license Ki.

rationale: Good parallel target-only arm and practical reporter-capacity qualification. However, categorical optical/reporter calls are not isolated by their readouts, the orthogonal method is under-validated, and simplified substrate-dependence rules overclassify mechanism. The limited direct substrate matrix is explicitly followed up, which earns partial credit.
reference_guardrails: D3 establishes spectral proximity, not the magnitude of inner filtering. Fluorophore-only signal loss does not distinguish absorption, quenching and chemical conversion.
Substrate-competitive inhibition is a kinetic subclass of target inhibition; it is not necessarily active-site occupancy. Substrate sequestration and chemical loss require separate controls.
Reporter-only inhibition and true target inhibition can coexist. Do not force mutually exclusive categories or subtract arbitrary effect percentages.

A fully validated staged reporter calibration can be informative; a specific analytical instrument is not mandatory. Target quenching, matrix matching, product recovery and chemical stability must justify the inference.
Orthogonal methods can have their own compound-dependent artifacts, including ion suppression. Nonfluorescence alone does not establish specificity.
Independent preparations/days support reproducibility; technical wells cannot substitute for them. A null significance test is not equivalence; margins should be scientifically justified.
Simple inner-filter correction formulas depend on optical geometry. For f=F_without/F_with, attenuation correction multiplies signal by f, not by 1/f.

The draft reference uses reporter Km as a preparation item, but full reporter Michaelis-Menten characterization is not universally essential if empirical capacity and relevant intermediate concentrations are validated.

No fixed concentrations, replicate counts, Z-prime or R-squared thresholds are supplied by the packet. Proposed pilot settings are acceptable when labeled and validated; they are not historical facts.
